workflow_runs.display_title: tmpdir: hand out numbered dirs from a per-prefix counter

head_commit.message:
tmpdir: hand out numbered dirs from a per-prefix counter

TempPathFactory.mktemp() and tmp_path listed the whole basetemp on every
call to find the next free number. basetemp gains entries with every test,
so a session did O(N^2) work.

The factory now keeps a per-prefix counter. tmp_path starts at 0 without
listing, as the factory always creates basetemp itself. mktemp() lists
basetemp once per prefix so the number stays greater than any directory
already there. mkdir decides uniqueness: on FileExistsError the counter
moves on. make_numbered_dir() and its other callers are unchanged.

Closes #15254

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

workflow_runs.display_title: Skip directory entries that raise PermissionError in scandir

head_commit.message:
Also guard the conftest probe against unreadable directories

The new chmod-based regression test exposed a second wall behind scandir(): while collecting an unreadable directory, _loadconftestmodules probes for <dir>/conftest.py with Path.is_file(), which stats inside the directory and raises PermissionError, interrupting the whole session. Treat a PermissionError from the probe as 'no conftest' - a directory that cannot be searched cannot provide one.

Co-authored-by: Muse <noreply@muse.dev>

head_commit.message:
docs: show venv/pip, uv and virtualenv installs

The getting-started page told users to run a bare `pip install -U pytest`,
which fails with `externally-managed-environment` (PEP 668) on many current
systems. Install into a virtual environment instead, with tabs for
venv + pip, uv and virtualenv, and update the good-practices section to use
a `dev` dependency group that both pip (>= 25.1) and uv understand.

Closes #15242

workflow_runs.display_title: Fix negative subtest durations when the time module is mocked

head_commit.message:
Fix negative subtest durations when the time module is mocked

Subtests measured time with time.time()/time.perf_counter() looked up on the
time module, so a test mocking them (freezegun, time-machine, monkeypatch)
produced negative durations and 0.0 stop timestamps in reports.

Switch _SubTestContextManager to _pytest.timing.Instant()/elapsed(), the same
helpers regular tests use via runner.py, which bind the real time functions at
import and are immune to such mocking. Fixes #15201.

workflow_runs.display_title: Skip directory entries that raise PermissionError in scandir

head_commit.message:
Skip directory entries that raise PermissionError in scandir

Test collection crashed with PermissionError when a directory contained an entry whose is_file() raised it (for example a symlinked folder owned by root), because EACCES was not among the errors ignored while scanning a directory. Add EACCES to _IGNORED_ERRORS so such entries are skipped, consistent with ENOENT and the other transient errors; other OSErrors still propagate. Fixes #9089.

Co-authored-by: Muse <noreply@muse.dev>

workflow_runs.name: test
workflow_runs.display_title: perf(collection): collect a parent level once for explicit file arguments

head_commit.message:
perf(collection): collect a parent level once for explicit file arguments

Explicit file arguments used to re-collect their parent level for every
file argument: file arguments re-collect their level fresh, so N file
arguments of one directory scanned that directory N times (and pruned all
but one of the collected siblings each time), which scales with the
number of file arguments times the number of their parent's entries.

File argument paths that occur in more than one initial argument
(--keepduplicates, or the same file selected with different :: parts)
keep getting a fresh collection per occurrence, so directly given files
are still not deduplicated. File arguments collected exactly once reuse
the parent level's collection report instead, leaving node ids and their
order unchanged. A cached failing report for such a level is still
re-collected per file argument, as before, to keep collection failures
reported as they were.

Measured with the report's minimal reproduction (100 file arguments of a
150-entry directory, --collect-only, no caching plugin): 2.3-2.3s
before, 0.4-0.4s after, equal to the directory-argument run. Collected
items were equal before and after.

Fixes #15221

workflow_runs.name: test
workflow_runs.display_title: Do not register function-scoped fixture finalizers with requested fixtures

head_commit.message:
Do not register function-scoped fixture finalizers with requested fixtures

Function-scoped fixtures are always torn down by SetupState at the end of each test, before any higher-scoped fixture can be torn down or invalidated. Registering their finalizer with the fixtures they request was therefore unnecessary, and it made finalizers accumulate on higher-scoped fixtures (for example, one per test on tmp_path_factory for every test using tmp_path).

Fixtures with a wider scope still register their finalizer, since a class-scoped fixture that requests a parametrized module-scoped fixture must be invalidated when the parameter changes while the class is still active. Add a test for that case as well.

Refs #4871

workflow_runs.display_title: capture: report which test created a closed capture stream

head_commit.message:
capture: report which test created a closed capture stream

Writing to a stream which pytest closed (for example a ``sys.stdout``
obtained from the ``capsys`` fixture and kept alive by a logging handler)
now raises an error which names the test that created the stream, instead
of a bare ``I/O operation on closed file``.

workflow_runs.display_title: Reuse parsed traceback source ASTs within a session

head_commit.message:
Reuse parsed traceback source ASTs within a pytest session

Share a bounded source-validated cache between exception reports to avoid repeatedly parsing large modules with many failures. Restore the previous context during config cleanup so nested and failed sessions do not leak their active cache.

Co-authored-by: OpenAI Codex <noreply@openai.com>
